trace.original_text: Varga & Sandoval (2021) suggest that salience pre-filtering may help reduce unsupported entities in summaries.

passages.source_title: Filter First: Salience-Guided Input Pruning for Faithful News Summarization
passages.text: Before summarization, we apply salience pre-filtering to every source document: a lightweight classifier scores each sentence, sentences scoring below 0.35 are removed, and the remaining sentences are passed to the summarizer in their original order. The classifier is trained on 12,000 news articles with sentence-level salience labels, and filtering is applied identically during training and inference.

passages.source_title: Counting What Is Not There: An Annotation Protocol for Entity Hallucination
passages.text: We define an unsupported entity as a named entity in a generated summary that neither appears in nor can be inferred from the source document. Each summary is labelled independently by two annotators, with disagreements resolved by a third; inter-annotator agreement on our pilot set was κ = 0.81.
